properties.description: Waters designated as Outstanding or Exceptional Resource Waters (ORW or ERW) are surface waters which provide outstanding recreational opportunities, support valuable fisheries and wildlife habitat, have good water quality, and are not significantly impacted by human activities. An outstanding resource water is a lake, stream or flowage having excellent water quality, high recreational and aesthetic value and high-quality fishing. ORW waters are free from point source or nonpoint source pollution. An exceptional resource water is a lake, stream, or flowage exhibiting the same high-quality resource values as outstanding waters but may be affected by point source pollution or have the potential for future discharge from a small sewer community. These designations are intended to meet federal Clean Water Act obligations requiring Wisconsin to adopt an “antidegradation” policy that is designed to prevent any lowering of water quality – especially in those waters having significant ecological or cultural value. This layer contains information on ORW and ERW lakes but not streams.

properties.snippet: Wisconsin's Water Management Units represent a delineation of basins in the state.
properties.description:
Wisconsin's Water Management Units data layer contains 24 delineated basins created initially for the Priority Watershed Program. Basins and watersheds are interconnected areas of land draining from surrounding ridge tops to a common point such as a lake or confluence with a neighboring land area.

 

These basins, delineated by DNR, generally indicate areas that drain into a common river system or lake, but may also be based on DNR basin management criteria.

properties.snippet: Wisconsin's Outstanding and Exceptional Rivers and Streams
properties.description: Wisconsin's Outstanding and Exceptional Resource Water (OERW) designations are designed to include Wisconsin's cleanest waters. The OERW dataset was first developed in the 1990s using narrative descriptions from the state’s OERW designations described in NR102 and the state’s 1:24,000 scale hydrography dataset using 7.5 minute USGS topographic quadrangle maps. The OERW spatial data quality has been reviewed by GIS specialists working with biological field staff and using more detailed landmarks and data over time. The accuracy of the delineations continue to improve with the use of improved technologies and tools. Year 2006 designations were derived by selecting and copying applicable features from the 1:24,000 scale hydrography dataset.

properties.snippet: The approximate thickness of unconsolidated materials as well as the approximate distribution of the Silurian bedrock in eastern Wisconsin.
properties.description:
This layer represents the approximate thickness of unconsolidated materials as well as the approximate distribution of the Silurian bedrock in eastern Wisconsin. It a composite of 8 WGNHS published maps which range in having a scale of 1:100,000 to 1:1,000,000. This layer was developed in 2017 and updated in 2022, however the sources used to develop it were published in 1978, 1979, 1982, 2004, 2011, 2013, 2019 and 2021.

This layer is part of the 2016-2018 NR 151 target performance standard rule revision. This layer was developed to assist the agricultural community in Wisconsin in maintain compliance with the NR 151 targeted performance standard. It is not recommended to be used for well installation, placement of utility lines, or any other construction or siting practice.

properties.title: Silurian Thickness of Unconsolidated Materials
properties.accessInformation:
The compilation of data sources into a single layer was completed by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resource’s Runoff Management Program.  GIS data was provided by Peter Schoephoester (Wisconsin Geologic and Natural History Survey) and John Luczaj (UW-Green Bay).  The final layer is based on the following publications:
•	Sherrill, M. G., 1978, ‘Geology and Ground Water in Door County, Wisconsin, with Emphasis on Contamination Potential in the Silurian Dolomite’, Plate 2, page 26, Surficial Geology, Infiltration and Runoff Potential, and Thickness of Unconsolidated Deposits, Door County, Wisconsin
•	Sherrill, M. G., 1979, ‘Contamination Potential in the Silurian Dolomite Aquifer, Eastern Wisconsin’, Thickness of Unconsolidated Materials
•	Mudrey, Jr., M. G., Brown, B. A., and Greenberg, J. K., 1982 ‘Bedrock Geologic Map of Wisconsin’, 
•	Evans, T. J., Massie-Ferch, K. M., and Peters, R. M., 2004, ‘Preliminary bedrock geologic map of Walworth, Racine, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Waukesha, Ozaukee, and Washington Counties’ Open-File Report 2004-18
•	Luczaj, John A., 2011, ‘Preliminary Geologic Map of the Buried Bedrock Surface, Brown County, Wisconsin’ Open-File Report 2011-02
•	McLaughlin, Patrick I., 2013, ‘Preliminary bedrock geology of Sheboygan County, Wisconsin’ Open-File Report 2013-03

candidates.title: Landsat Summer Water Clarity Data – 2017 - Path Date Index

properties.snippet: Link to path date index shapefile for the Landsat Summer Water Clarity Data – 2017 raster dataset.
properties.description:
Path date index shapefile for the Landsat Summer Water Clarity Data - 2017 raster dataset.   The State of Wisconsin is represented by four different paths of the Landsat reference system and the images for these paths are acquired 2, 7, and 9 days apart. This means the combined summer water clarity maps take four different dates to produce an annual summer water clarity composite for Wisconsin. Therefore, the water clarity dataset represents the combined water clarity maps for four different dates mosaicked from Lake Michigan in the eastern part of the state to the Mississippi River in the western part of the state. There are some areas where two paths overlap and a single lake might include data from two different dates. The Summer Water Clarity Path Date Index shapefile represents a list of these dates.

For more information, please visit the Wisconsin DNR's Remote sensing of water quality web page.   Please contact the WI DNR Water Quality Program (dnrlakeb@wisconsin.gov) to request additional datasets.
